title: Suspending Shared PMD Permits Until Riding Culture Improves
what_it_is: Suspending Shared PMD Permits Until Riding Culture Improves

sections.label: E-scooter registration and penalties
sections.summary: From the second half of 2018, all e-scooters must be registered with identification stickers, and errant users face strict penalties under the Active Mobility Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: When implemented in the second half of 2018, all e-scooters, regardless of whether they are privately-owned or shared, must be registered and have identification stickers prominently pasted on them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Under the Active Mobility Act which commenced on 1 May 2018, errant users of e-scooters are also subject to strict penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We do not rule out starting a licensing regime for PMD-sharing services at a later phase.

sections.label: LTA Safety Riding Programme
sections.summary: LTA started a Safety Riding Programme in February this year to educate participants on safe riding practices and rules under the Active Mobility Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: At the same time, LTA has also started a Safety Riding Programme since February this year to educate the participants on safe riding practices as well as the rules and conduct under the Active Mobility Act.

sections.label: Mobile CCTV trial for errant riding
sections.summary: LTA has embarked on a trial to study mobile CCTV cameras in identifying and reducing errant riding behaviour along public paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Thirdly, LTA is also adopting innovative solutions to manage this situation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have embarked on a trial to study the effectiveness of mobile closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in identifying and reducing errant riding behaviour along public paths.

sections.label: Rising accidents and advisory panel review
sections.summary: Reported accidents rose from 19 in 2015 to 42 in 2016 and 128 in 2017, prompting the Active Mobility Advisory Panel to review measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Just to give some statistics, in 2015, we have about 19 cases of reported accidents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: And that has increased to 42 in 2016, and 128 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This is quite a significant increase and we are quite concerned about it as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: And in light of the increase in active mobility-related accidents, we have also engaged the Active Mobility Advisory Panel to review some of the measures that need to be taken, such as the reduction of speed limits on footpaths, whether there is a need for the usage of helmets, and there are also suggestions to dismount and push at traffic crossings, bus stops as well as in crowded areas, and suggestions on the insurance and compensation framework as well.

sections.label: Safe Riding Programme start date
sections.summary: The Safe Riding Programme has only started in February this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With regard to public education, the Safe Riding Programme has only started in February this year.

sections.label: Active Mobility Act as deterrent
sections.summary: The Active Mobility Act has been in force since May and will serve as a strong deterrent for users who ride irresponsibly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: At the same time, with the Active Mobility Act being in force since May, I think that will actually serve as a strong deterrent factor for users who ride irresponsibly.
